group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
A 71-year-old woman was driven to the emergency department by her son early this morning after three days of progressively wetter cough, low-grade chills, and a new band of dull right-sided chest discomfort that sharpens whenever she takes a deeper breath; she purposefully skipped her usual morning prescriptions of carvedilol, furosemide, lisinopril, and low-dose aspirin so that clinicians could observe her unmodified physiology, and she declined the acetaminophen her husband offered at home. Her background is notable for a remote lacunar infarct six years ago that left no motor deficit, a longstanding dilated cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction last documented at 35 % on an outpatient echocardiogram four months earlier, well-controlled hypertension, and mild diet-controlled type 2 diabetes; she has never required dialysis, never carried a chronic liver diagnosis, and her primary physician’s notes list normal baseline renal indices and transaminases. She has never been diagnosed with any form of cancer. She lives with her spouse in a single-story house, gardens on weekends, and drives herself to a weekly bridge group; she has never resided in an extended-care facility. The patient quit a 10-pack-year cigarette habit three decades ago, drinks a single glass of wine on special occasions, and denies recreational drug use. State records confirm receipt of both pneumococcal vaccines and the current season’s influenza shot. On arrival she sat upright on the stretcher, conversing in complete sentences, correctly stating the date, location, and reason for evaluation, and recalling three objects at five minutes, indicating intact cognition. Nursing triage documented untreated vital signs on room air at this near-sea-level hospital: oral temperature 38.0 °C, regular tachycardic pulse 112 beats min⁻¹ confirmed on three-lead telemetry, automated right-arm blood pressure 118/68 mm Hg verified by manual cuff, respirations counted for a full minute at 24 breaths min⁻¹ with mild intercostal effort but no nasal flaring, and fingertip pulse oximetry ranging between 90 % and 91 % while seated. Skin appeared warm and lightly diaphoretic yet capillary refill was under two seconds; conjunctivae were injected but not icteric, and no peripheral edema beyond the trace ankle pitting that her cardiologist labels chronic. Jugular venous pulsation hovered at the level of the clavicle in the semi-upright position, matching outpatient notes. Cardiac auscultation revealed a crisp S1/S2 with a soft third sound but no new murmur or pericardial rub. Lung examination demonstrated coarse inspiratory crackles over the right mid-axillary and posterior lower zones with preserved resonance to percussion; the left lung transmitted vesicular breath sounds throughout, and no dull stony note or shifting percussion suggested free fluid in either costophrenic recess. The abdomen was soft and nontender with normal bowel sounds and no organomegaly. A focused neurologic screen showed equal reactive pupils, intact extra-ocular movements, 5/5 strength in all extremities, and normal rapid alternating movements. Finger-stick glucose obtained prior to vascular access read 122 mg dL⁻¹. Peripheral venous and right radial arterial samples were drawn within ten minutes of bay entry—before any intravenous crystalloids, antimicrobial therapy, bronchodilators, diuretics, or supplemental oxygen beyond the 2 mL heparinized saline used to lock the arterial line. Basic metabolic panel returned sodium 137 mEq L⁻¹, potassium 4.1 mEq L⁻¹, chloride 103 mEq L⁻¹, bicarbonate 22 mEq L⁻¹, blood urea nitrogen 26 mg dL⁻¹, and creatinine 0.9 mg dL⁻¹, consistent with her outpatient figures. Complete blood count showed leukocytosis to 13.1 × 10⁹ L⁻¹ with 87 % segmented neutrophils, hematocrit 40 %, hemoglobin 13.2 g dL⁻¹, and platelet count 236 × 10⁹ L⁻¹. The arterial blood gas obtained while she remained on room air revealed pH 7.35, PaCO₂ 35 mm Hg, PaO₂ 72 mm Hg, and calculated bicarbonate 19 mEq L⁻¹, signifying mild hypoxemia with near-physiologic acid–base status. Serum lactate was 1.7 mmol L⁻¹, and high-sensitivity troponin I remained below the analytical threshold. A portable postero-anterior chest radiograph obtained before any therapy showed a dense consolidation involving the right lower lobe with prominent air bronchograms; diaphragmatic outlines and costophrenic angles were sharp, and there was no layering opacity or meniscus sign to suggest fluid accumulation. Cardiothoracic ratio appeared unchanged from a film last year. Twelve-lead electrocardiography displayed sinus tachycardia at 110 beats min⁻¹ with left-bundle branch block morphology identical to prior tracings and no acute ischemic pattern. Two sets of peripheral blood cultures, an induced sputum specimen for Gram stain and culture, urinary antigens for Streptococcus pneumoniae and Legionella pneumophila, and a respiratory viral PCR panel were dispatched to the laboratory prior to any empirical medication. Up to the moment this narrative is entered, the patient has received no intravenous fluids, vasopressors, antipyretics, bronchodilators, diuretics, corticosteroids, or supplemental oxygen, ensuring that every vital sign, laboratory value, and imaging finding above reflects her untreated presentation physiology.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) adds demographic, comorbidity, examination, laboratory, and radiographic points at presentation.
- Demographics: for a woman, start with age minus 10: 71 − 10 = 61. She lives at home, so no nursing-home points (+0).
- Comorbidities: systolic heart failure (dilated cardiomyopathy, EF 35%) = +10; cerebrovascular disease (prior lacunar infarct) = +10. No malignancy, liver disease, or renal disease = +0 each. Hypertension and diabetes do not score separately.
- Examination: no altered mental status (+0); RR 24 is below 30 (+0); systolic BP 118 is not below 90 (+0); temperature 38.0°C is neither <35 nor ≥40 (+0); pulse 112 is below 125 (+0).
- Laboratory criteria: arterial pH 7.35 is not <7.35 (+0); BUN 26 is below 30 mg/dL (+0); sodium 137 is not <130 mEq/L (+0); glucose 122 is below 250 mg/dL (+0); hematocrit 40% is not <30% (+0). Room-air PaO₂ 72 mm Hg is not <60, and saturation 90–91% is not <90% (+0).
- Radiograph: consolidation but no pleural effusion (+0).
Sum: 61 + 10 + 10 = 81 (PSI class III).
Final answer: 81
